To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The bronchial epithelial cells are a major target of environmental pollutants and allergens.

1) the bronchial airway epithelium is the site of the initial interaction of environmental stimuli (allergens, pollutants and infections) with the susceptible genotype; 2) the epithelial response is a complex and coordinated series of events that includes the production of chemotactic factors for the recruitment of inflammatory cells; and 3) the epithelium plays a key role in the regulation of the immune response and airway remodelling.
the epithelium in asthma is damaged by environmental agents and the repair response to this injury is a major contributor to the pathophysiology of the asthmatics state.
In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding the mechanisms of epithelial cell injury, the consequences of the epithelial cell shedding, the mechanisms of epithelium regeneration and how the repair process is influenced by genetic susceptibility and environmental exposures.
the role of the bronchial airway epithelium in the pathogenesis of asthma.
the epithelial cell and its interactions with the airway laryngeal epithelial cell and airway smooth muscle cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bronchial mucosa is damaged and that repair is abnormal.
the bronchial asthma is a chronic inflammatory disease of the airways, which is characterised by a complex interplay between genetic and environmental factors.
asthma is a disease of the epithelium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the epithelial barrier is compromised and that this leads to a proinflammatory state.
the bronchial asthma phenotype is a consequence of a complex interplay between the bronchial airway epithelium and the immune system.
the airway epithelium is a key player in orchestrating the development and maintenance phase of asthma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bronchial airway epithelium is not just an inert lining, but rather an integral part of the immune system, with the ability to sense and respond to a range of environmental insults.
epithelial shedding is a major contributor to the asthmatic inflammatory process and the subsequent remodelling.
the epithelium, in particular the airway basal cells, are key to the initiation and maintenance of asthma.
